title: The Odyssey: Odysseus and the Cyclops
author: Homer
intro: Depois da guerra de Tróia, Ulisses tenta voltar a casa. Neste episódio, a inteligência vence a força bruta, mas o orgulho custa caro.

B2.text: After the Trojan War, Odysseus and his men sail home, but they are blown off course and land on an island. They enter a cave full of cheese and sheep. Its owner is Polyphemus, a giant Cyclops with one eye. He traps the men inside with a huge rock and begins to eat them. Odysseus is clever. He tells the giant that his name is 'Nobody' and gives him strong wine. When the Cyclops falls asleep, the men blind him with a sharpened stick. He screams that 'Nobody' is hurting him, so the other giants do not come to help. In the morning, the men escape, hidden under the sheep.

questions.q: What do the men use to blind the Cyclops?
options: A stone
A burning house
A sword
A sharpened stick
to teach someone a lesson
to keep someone inside so that they cannot leave
to help someone escape
to give someone a present
questions.why: O gigante prende os homens dentro da gruta com uma pedra enorme.

questions.q: Why does Odysseus say his name is 'Nobody'?
options: The giant asked for a secret name
So that the other giants will not understand who is attacking
To make the giant laugh
He is ashamed of his real name
questions.why: Quando o gigante grita, os outros ouvem que 'ninguém' o ataca.

options: The giant falls asleep, then he is blinded, then Odysseus offers wine
Odysseus gives the giant wine, the giant falls asleep, the men blind him, the men escape under the sheep
The men escape under the sheep, then they blind the giant, then Odysseus gives him wine
The men blind the giant, then they give him wine, then he falls asleep
questions.why: Vinho, sono, cegueira e fuga debaixo das ovelhas: é esta a ordem do texto.

questions.q: What does the story suggest about how Odysseus solves problems?
options: He prefers cleverness to open fighting
He asks the other giants for help
He relies only on his strength
He waits for the gods to act
questions.why: Usa um nome falso e vinho em vez de lutar de frente.

B2.discussion: Is Odysseus a hero because he is clever or because he is strong? What qualities make a hero today?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Retell the escape from the cave as if you were one of Odysseus's men.

C1.text: Having survived the war at Troy, Odysseus finds himself, through a combination of misfortune and his own curiosity, imprisoned in the cave of the Cyclops Polyphemus. Rather than resort to brute force, which would leave the entrance sealed and the men doomed, he relies on cunning. He offers the giant undiluted wine and, when asked his name, replies 'Nobody'. Once Polyphemus is drunk and asleep, the Greeks drive a burning stake into his single eye. His neighbours, alerted by his cries that 'Nobody' is attacking him, dismiss the matter as a private affliction. The pun secures their escape, yet Odysseus's pride, when he later taunts the blinded giant with his real name, provokes the wrath of Poseidon.

questions.q: What do the Greeks do once Polyphemus is drunk and asleep?
options: They wake him and negotiate
They roll the rock away and flee
They drive a burning stake into his single eye
They tie him up with rope
questions.why: Cravam-lhe uma estaca em brasa no único olho.

questions.q: 'Dismiss the matter as a private affliction' means the neighbours
options: investigate the cause carefully
celebrate his misfortune
punish him for his cries
treat his suffering as a personal problem that needs no action
questions.why: 'Affliction' é um sofrimento; 'dismiss' é não lhe dar importância.

questions.q: Why does Odysseus not simply kill the giant by force?
options: He is too tired
He respects the giant
Killing him would leave the entrance sealed and the men trapped
He has no weapons
questions.why: Sem o gigante vivo, ninguém desloca a pedra da entrada.

questions.q: What is the effect of the name 'Nobody'?
options: It makes the giant sleep
The Cyclops forgives him
The giants fear Odysseus
The neighbours misread the cries and do not help
questions.why: Os vizinhos interpretam mal os gritos e não ajudam.

questions.q: What does the last sentence suggest about Odysseus?
options: He never makes mistakes
He fears the gods
His cleverness is accompanied by a pride that has consequences
He is always humble
questions.why: O orgulho ao revelar o nome verdadeiro provoca a ira de Poseidon.

C1.discussion: The Odyssey praises cunning as a virtue, yet punishes pride. Can intelligence be a moral quality?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Analyse how the story links cleverness and pride.

C2.text: The Cyclops episode is often read as a study in the tension between civilisation and its absence. Polyphemus, who neither farms nor honours the laws of hospitality, violates precisely the customs on which Greek society rests; Odysseus, by contrast, meets savagery with a trickery that is itself ethically ambivalent. His pseudonym is a linguistic conceit that plays on the Greek for 'no one' and the word for 'cunning', so that the hero's intelligence and his self-erasure coincide. Yet the victory carries a price. By abandoning anonymity to boast of his triumph, Odysseus reasserts the very ego he had concealed, and the ensuing curse condemns him to years of wandering, a reminder that in Homeric epic, brilliance unaccompanied by restraint invites divine retribution.

questions.q: Which customs does Polyphemus violate, according to the passage?
options: The custom of sacrificing to Poseidon
The rules of naval warfare
The duty to honour the dead
The laws of hospitality
questions.why: O texto diz que não honra as leis da hospitalidade.

questions.q: 'Ethically ambivalent' trickery means that Odysseus's deceit
options: is clearly wrong
is a sign of weakness
is effective but not morally clear-cut
is forbidden by the gods
questions.why: Funciona, mas não é moralmente simples.

questions.q: Why does the writer say Odysseus 'reasserts the very ego he had concealed'?
options: By boasting under his real name he stops being 'Nobody' and draws attention to himself
He gives the giant a gift
He forgets his own name
He hides in the cave again
questions.why: Ao revelar o nome deixa de ser 'ninguém' e volta a afirmar o seu ego.

questions.q: What does 'the hero's intelligence and his self-erasure coincide' mean here?
options: The same trick shows his cleverness and makes him 'no one'
His cleverness and his strength are equal
He erases his mistakes with intelligence
He is both wise and forgetful
questions.why: O pseudónimo mostra a sua inteligência e, ao mesmo tempo, apaga-o.

questions.q: What general lesson does the final clause draw?
options: The gods always reward intelligence
Anonymity is always dangerous
Civilised societies never punish
Brilliance without self-control can bring punishment
questions.why: 'Brilliance unaccompanied by restraint invites divine retribution.'

C2.discussion: Is deceit justified when used against someone who behaves savagely?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Discuss the view that Odysseus's greatest enemy is his own pride.
